nrIncident.summary: Disruption in the Barking area until at least the end of the day on Monday 26 October: amended Suffragette line service, and no trains between Barking and Grays via Rainham
nrIncident.routes:
c2c through Barking
London Overground between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside
nrIncident.message:
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, blocking some lines.
Some trains through Barking will be cancelled or revised as a result. Where trains do run there may be delays of up to 10 minutes in the area.
• London Overground are running a reduced half hourly service on the Suffragette line between Gospel Oak and Barking. No trains will run between Barking and Barking Riverside.
• There will be no c2c service between Barking and Grays via Dagenham Dock, Rainham (Essex) and Purfleet
• c2c services that run to London Liverpool Street will instead to be diverted to London Fenchurch Street - please be aware that there has been a late notice change to the engineering work that was scheduled to take place between London Fenchurch Street and Barking
Disruption is expected until at least the end of the day on Monday 26 October.
A visual disruption map video is available.
c2c customer advice:
What's Happened?
A freight train has derailed between Woodgrange Park and Barking, which means platforms 7 and 8 at Barking station are blocked.
How does this affect my journey?
No services are calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet. Please expect delays and service alterations.
Services to / from London Liverpool Street via Stratford (London) will instead run to / from London Fenchurch Street via West Ham. London Liverpool Street and London Fenchurch Street are a short distance apart.
Your ticket will be accepted at no extra cost on:
• First Essex buses between Purfleet and Grays
• Greater Anglia between London Liverpool Street and Southend Victoria
• London Buses between Barking, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet and Grays
• London Buses Superloop SL12
• London Underground District line between Barking and Upminster, and Jubilee line between West Ham and Stratford (London)
Replacement buses are running half hourly between Barking and Grays, calling at Rainham, Dagenham Dock, Rainham, Purfleet.
What should I do?
Please check before you travel and allow extra time for your journey. c2c are working to keep customers moving and will provide details of any alternative travel arrangements as soon as they are confirmed.
If your journey is significantly delayed or cancelled, you may wish to travel later when services are running more normally.
London Overground customer advice:
Service is suspended between Barking and Barking Riverside.
Your ticket can be used, at no extra cost, on London Buses via any reasonable route in order to complete your journey.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Storm Boelo - disruption to LNER services in Scotland and northern England today
nrIncident.routes: Various routes across the LNER network
nrIncident.message:
Storm Boelo has been named by the Met Office. Amber and yellow weather warnings have been issued across Scotland and northern England on Sunday 25 October. LNER have made some pre-planned alterations to their services north of Northallerton and Darlington today. There may be further changes to service levels across the LNER network depending on the impact of Storm Boelo.
Today, Sunday 25 October you are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption.
Across the rest of the LNER network, you are strongly encouraged to check your journey before travelling and allow extra time where possible.
Service impact:
Today, Sunday 25 October
• Trains are expected to run normally between London Kings Cross and Doncaster / Leeds
• A reduced service of one train per hour is running between Northallerton / Darlington and Newcastle / Edinburgh, with short notice delays and alterations also possible
• Trains between Northallerton and Durham will run at reduced speeds
• All LNER services to and from Aberdeen, with the exception of the 13:47 Aberdeen to Edinburgh service, will be cancelled
• LNER services will continue running to and from Inverness, with short notice delays possible
Due to the severity of the weather and expected road closures, rail replacement coaches will not be available between Edinburgh and Aberdeen. As other operators are also impacted, it will not be possible to travel with a different train company.
Ticket easements:
Customers are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption. Tickets for LNER services to and from Aberdeen and stations in between Edinburgh and Aberdeen dated Sunday 25 October can be used on alternative LNER services between from today up to and including Tuesday 27 October.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Trains may be delayed through the Bedhampton area, as they must travel at reduced speed due to a signal fault.
Railway signals warn drivers when they need to stop. Normally, a green light means the track is clear, while yellow signals warn of a red light ahead.
Signalling works on "fail-safe" principles. If a signal cannot change properly, it defaults to a more restrictive setting, causing trains to slow down even if the track is clear.
Network Rail maintains the system, and work is being done with them to fix the fault as quickly as possible.

Network Rail maintains the system, and work is being done with them to fix the fault as quickly as possible.

nrIncident.message:
Storm Boelo has been named by the Met Office. Amber and yellow weather warnings have been issued across Scotland and northern England on Sunday 25 October. LNER have made some pre-planned alterations to their services north of Northallerton and Darlington today. There may be further changes to service levels across the LNER network depending on the impact of Storm Boelo.
Today, Sunday 25 October you are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption.
Across the rest of the LNER network, you are strongly encouraged to check your journey before travelling and allow extra time where possible.
Service impact:
Currently disruptions:
Peterborough - expected until 16:00
Services through Peterborough are disrupted due to a tree on the line. Services may be delayed by up to 40 minutes.
You may use Great Northern or Thameslink services between Peterborough and London Kings Cross at no extra cost.
Today, Sunday 25 October
• Trains are expected to run normally between London Kings Cross and Doncaster / Leeds
• A reduced service of one train per hour is running between Northallerton / Darlington and Newcastle / Edinburgh, with short notice delays and alterations also possible
• Trains between Northallerton and Durham will run at reduced speeds
• All LNER services to and from Aberdeen, with the exception of the 13:47 Aberdeen to Edinburgh service, will be cancelled
• LNER services will continue running to and from Inverness, with short notice delays possible
Due to the severity of the weather and expected road closures, rail replacement coaches will not be available between Edinburgh and Aberdeen. As other operators are also impacted, it will not be possible to travel with a different train company.
Ticket easements:
Customers are advised not to travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen in either direction due to expected disruption. Tickets for LNER services to and from Aberdeen and stations in between Edinburgh and Aberdeen dated Sunday 25 October can be used on alternative LNER services between from today up to and including Tuesday 27 October.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

Today, Sunday 25 October

• Liverpool Lime Street to Glasgow Central, in both directions
• Manchester Airport to Glasgow Central and Edinburgh in both directions
No rail replacement transport will be provided on this route.
Services on other routes

Please note other train companies and transport operators will also be affected by these weather warnings.

Storm Boelo has been named by the Met Office. Amber and yellow weather warnings have been issued across Scotland and northern England on Sunday 25 October. LNER have made some pre-planned alterations to their services north of Northallerton and Darlington today. There may be further changes to service levels across the LNER network depending on the impact of Storm Boelo.

Across the rest of the LNER network, you are strongly encouraged to check your journey before travelling and allow extra time where possible.
Service impact:
Currently disruptions:
Peterborough - expected until 17:00
An earlier tree on the line at Peterborough is causing residual delays to services through Peterborough. Trains running through this station may be delayed by up to 60 minutes.
Today, Sunday 25 October
• Trains are expected to run normally between London Kings Cross and Doncaster / Leeds
• A reduced service of one train per hour is running between Northallerton / Darlington and Newcastle / Edinburgh, with short notice delays and alterations also possible

If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.

Today, Sunday 25 October you are advised to only travel if your journey is essential.

Between Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street - expected until the end of the day
Lines have reopened following a tree blocking the line between Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street Trains running between these stations will still be cancelled, severely delayed or be revised to terminate and start back from alternative stations.
TransPennine Express are advising customers not to travel between Manchester Piccadilly / Manchester Victoria and Liverpool Limes Street in both directions.

Today, Sunday 25 October

TransPennine Express services will not operate on the following routes on Sunday 25 October
• Liverpool Lime Street to Glasgow Central, in both directions
• Manchester Airport to Glasgow Central and Edinburgh in both directions
No rail replacement transport will be provided on this route.
Services on other routes
Services will also be severely impacted on other routes of the TransPennine Express network, with late notice delays and cancellations expected and rail replacement transport may not be available.
Major Engineering work is also taking place in the York area. Replacement transport operating for this engineering work may also see delays and other disruption due to expected road conditions.

TransPennine Express services will not be operating on the West Coast Main Line in both directions.
As a result, it is advised not to travel on this route. There are no trains or rail replacement buses running between Manchester Airport and Glasgow Central / Edinburgh, and Liverpool Lime Street and Glasgow Central in both directions.
Customers on all other TransPennine Express routes are advised to travel only for essential journeys as rail replacement transport may not be available in the event of further disruption.
Please note other train companies and transport operators will also be affected by these weather warnings.
Ticket easements and refunds:
If you have a ticket dated for travel on Sunday 25 October, you can use it on any TransPennine Express service on Monday 26 or Tuesday 27 October at no extra cost. You do not need to buy a new ticket.

nrIncident.summary: Storm Boelo - disruption to TransPennine Express services today: essential travel only
nrIncident.routes: Various routes across the TransPennine Express network
nrIncident.message:
Storm Boelo has been named by the Met Office. Amber and yellow weather warnings have been issued across Scotland and northern England today. TransPennine Express have made some pre-planned alterations to their services north of Carlisle on today. There may be further changes to service levels across the TransPennine Express network depending on the impact of Storm Boelo.
Today, Sunday 25 October you are advised to only travel if your journey is essential.
Service impact:
Today, Sunday 25 October
How will this affect my journey?
TransPennine Express services will not operate on the following routes on Sunday 25 October
• Liverpool Lime Street to Glasgow Central, in both directions
• Manchester Airport to Glasgow Central and Edinburgh in both directions
No rail replacement transport will be provided on this route.
Services on other routes
Services will also be severely impacted on other routes of the TransPennine Express network, with late notice delays and cancellations expected and rail replacement transport may not be available.
Major Engineering work is also taking place in the York area. Replacement transport operating for this engineering work may also see delays and other disruption due to expected road conditions.
What should I do?
TransPennine Express services will not be operating on the West Coast Main Line in both directions.
As a result, it is advised not to travel on this route. There are no trains or rail replacement buses running between Manchester Airport and Glasgow Central / Edinburgh, and Liverpool Lime Street and Glasgow Central in both directions.
Customers on all other TransPennine Express routes are advised to travel only for essential journeys as rail replacement transport may not be available in the event of further disruption.
Please note other train companies and transport operators will also be affected by these weather warnings.
Ticket easements and refunds:
If you have a ticket dated for travel on Sunday 25 October, you can use it on any TransPennine Express service on Monday 26 or Tuesday 27 October at no extra cost. You do not need to buy a new ticket.
Customers with tickets dated today, Sunday 25 October, arrangements have been made for you to use your ticket to travel on the limited Avanti West Coast services that are running on Sunday between Preston, Carlisle and Edinburgh / Glasgow at no extra cost and Avanti West Coast customers can also use their tickets to travel on TransPennine Express services between these destinations (where applicable). Please bear in mind the services that do run may be delayed or cancelled at short notice and you may experience overcrowding.
If your intended train is cancelled or you’re unable to complete your journey, you can apply for a refund from the retailer you purchased your ticket from.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
